chunks: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿUthmān al-Aʿwar narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who is killed, and his head is found in one tribe, his middle, chest, and hands in another tribe, and the rest of him in another tribe, he said: "His diyah is upon the people in whose tribe his chest and hands are found, and the funeral prayer is upon him there."
ai.seo_question: If a murdered person's body parts are found in different places, which group is responsible for the diyah and funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a murdered person whose body parts are found in different tribal territories. It places the diyah liability and the funeral prayer in relation to the location where the chest and hands are found, indicating the juridical importance of the principal body section in rulings concerning the deceased.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.484 - Al-Fadl ibn 'Uthman al-A'war narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) and him from his father, Imam al-Baqir, regarding a man who is killed and his head is found in one tribe, his torso and hands in another tribe, and the rest of his body in a different tribe.
The Imam said: "The responsibility for his blood money (diyah) is upon the tribe where his torso and hands are found, and the funeral prayer should be performed over those parts”.
